lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Supervised application: transport and logistics over time

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic transport and logistics over time task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner drafts a fictional month's plan for getting to a fictional job or set of appointments using realistic transport modes for their actual situation (which might include walking, public transit, rideshare, a ride from someone, or biking — not assuming a personal car), then reviews it with an adult who checks feasibility and suggests at least one backup option.
safetyNotes: The plan does not assume the learner has, or will have, a personal vehicle; any realistic combination of transport modes is acceptable.
No real ride-share account, real payment method, or real trip is required — the plan and its review are entirely on paper.

simulationAlternative.description: If no adult is available for a live review today, the learner self-checks the plan against a provided feasibility checklist (does every leg have a named mode, a backup for at least one leg, and a plan for bad weather or a missed connection) and notes any item the checklist flags.

materials: learner-local: paper or a notes document

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Which single leg of your plan is most likely to fail on a bad day, and does your backup for it actually work?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u02-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Plan realism: The plan uses realistic modes and includes at least one backup for at least one leg. | Review integration: The revision directly addresses something the review or self-check identified. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner redraft the plan assuming their primary transport mode becomes unavailable for one full week, and show how the fictional month's plan adapts.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic transport and logistics over time task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

localMaterials.label: paper or a notes document
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: transport and logistics over time worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner drafts a fictional month's plan for getting to a fictional job or set of appointments using realistic transport modes for their actual situation (which might include walking, public transit, rideshare, a ride from someone, or biking — not assuming a personal car), then reviews it with an adult who checks feasibility and suggests at least one backup option.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact transport and logistics over time decision or action.
Model move 2: Before drafting, list every transport mode that's realistically available to you, even ones you don't usually use.
Model move 3: Draft the fictional month's transport plan, then review it with an adult for feasibility.

Model check: Plan realism: The plan uses realistic modes and includes at least one backup for at least one leg. | Review integration: The revision directly addresses something the review or self-check identified.

resources.title: transport and logistics over time action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for transport and logistics over time.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: transport and logistics over time coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner drafts a fictional month's plan for getting to a fictional job or set of appointments using realistic transport modes for their actual situation (which might include walking, public transit, rideshare, a ride from someone, or biking — not assuming a personal car), then reviews it with an adult who checks feasibility and suggests at least one backup option.
Coach direction: Before drafting, list every transport mode that's realistically available to you, even ones you don't usually use.

Learner prompt: List every transport mode that is realistically available to you or your fictional household (walking, transit, biking, rideshare, a ride from someone, etc.), even ones you wouldn't normally choose.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: transport and logistics over time complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Draft the fictional month's transport plan, then review it with an adult for feasibility.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I drafted a transport plan covering the fictional month's regular trips.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I reviewed the plan with an adult, or self-checked it against the provided feasibility checklist.
Response 3 (t2-p3): The plan includes at least one backup option for at least one leg of the trip.

Equal-access rule: If no adult is available for a live review today, the learner self-checks the plan against a provided feasibility checklist (does every leg have a named mode, a backup for at least one leg, and a plan for bad weather or a missed connection) and notes any item the checklist flags.

resources.title: transport and logistics over time minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which single leg of your plan is most likely to fail on a bad day, and does your backup for it actually work?

Success checks: Plan realism: The plan uses realistic modes and includes at least one backup for at least one leg. | Review integration: The revision directly addresses something the review or self-check identified.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: transport and logistics over time supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g12-u02-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional transport and logistics over time condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Plan realism: The plan uses realistic modes and includes at least one backup for at least one leg. | Review integration: The revision directly addresses something the review or self-check identified..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u02-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u02-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
